previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy (EF 20%), type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, chest pressure described as 'an aquarium on my chest,' and a 15-pound weight gain over two days. He presented with signs of acute on chronic systolic heart failure, including elevated BNP (5,314), moderate pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, and pitting edema. He was treated with an IV furosemide drip, initially at 10 mg/hr and increased to 13 mg/hr due to inadequate urine output. His weight decreased from 139 kg to 131.9 kg, and symptoms improved. He was transitioned to oral torsemide 80 mg AM and 40 mg PM, with addition of hydralazine and isosorbide mononitrate. Metoprolol was changed to 200 mg daily. His kidney function remained stable with creatinine up to 1.9. He was discharged home with services, weighing 131.9 kg, breathing comfortably, and with a plan for cardiology follow-up, including restarting losartan.

# Acute on Chronic Systolic Congestive Heart Failure: Patient 
presented with ___ chest pain/pressure along with frequent 
coughs, worsening lower extremity edema.  He was given twice 
daily boluses of furosemide (80-200mg) with good initial effect 
as his chest pain resolved, his cough and crackles resolved, and 
his lower extremity edema improved modestly.  He was continued 
on his home medications of metoprolol, spironolactone, 
isosorbide mononitrate, hydralazine, and digoxin; ___ 
therapy was considered but was deferred to his involved 
outpatient providers.  He had no vital sign or significant 
worsening of electrolytes during his hospital stay.  He was 
discharged as patient was getting angry about remaining in the 
hospital and wanted to go home.  He will be followed by an 
Atrius-affilitate nurse and ___ different visiting nurse network 
___ by previous one for noncompliance) who will call him 
every morning to encourage medication compliance.

# Coronary Artery Disease: Patient has chronically elevated trop 
in the setting of CKD. However, his value here is significantly 
higher than previously mild elevations suggesting there may be 
an acute ischemic component. This would fit with his history of 
missing clopidogrel doses over the past several days in the 
setting of ___ within the past half year. EKG is 
without ongoing ischemic changes.  Patient was maintained on 
home aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, nitroglycerin, and 
morphine for breakthrough pain.  No cardiac catheterization was 
performed (no EKG changes, unclear response to nitroglycerin, 
poor renal function, poor medication compliance would be a 
problem for stenting, poor surgical candidate).  Ultimately, his 
chest pain resolved with diuresis.

# Type II Diabetes Mellitus: Chronic issue ___ HbA1c was 10%. 
 HbA1c this hospital stay was 9.4%.  He was kept on his home 
insulin glargine 40mg along with an insulin lispro sliding 
scale.
